findings.finding: CMS (a component of HHS) granted all CMS employees access to its internally built chatbot, CMS Chat, using a voluntary waitlist to build early-adopter momentum before full rollout.
findings.estimated_users: 100% of CMS employees granted access (CMS headcount ~5,400-6,200); 4,700+ employees trained via the 'AI Ignite' micro-training program
findings.exact_quote: 100% of CMS employees have been granted access to use CMS Chat, with participation from all CMS components and the Office of the Administrator.
findings.source_title: CMS built a waitlist for its AI chatbot — and that drove momentum — official says | Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: Quote attributed to CMS Chief Technology Architect Andres Colón Pérez. Article also states 80% of users reported the tool helped them save time. CMS is an HHS component; recorded under HHS per the agencies table (no separate CMS row exists). Distinct from the existing 'HHS | ChatGPT (OpenAI)' entry (all-HHS OpenAI deployment) and 'HHS | ChIRP' (NIH-specific); CMS Chat is CMS's own internally built tool.

findings.tool_name: Agentforce (Salesforce AI agents — IRS Office of Chief Counsel, Taxpayer Advocate Service, Office of Appeals)
findings.finding: IRS deployed Salesforce's Agentforce AI agent platform to its Office of Chief Counsel, Taxpayer Advocate Service, and Office of Appeals for case summarization and search, explicitly framed as a response to steep IRS workforce cuts.
findings.estimated_users: Deployed to three IRS offices (Chief Counsel, Taxpayer Advocate Service, Office of Appeals); no published headcount for those offices specifically. Context: IRS-wide workforce fell from ~100,000 to ~75,000 during 2025.
findings.exact_quote: The AI system will be integrated into the Office of Chief Counsel, Taxpayer Advocate Services, and the Office of Appeals
findings.source_title: IRS Deploys Salesforce AI Agents Amid Major Workforce Reduction: Report | Techstrong.ai
findings.notes: Originally reported by Axios (2025-11-21); the Axios URL returned HTTP 403 on fetch, so this cites Techstrong.ai's contemporaneous republish carrying matching verbatim text. IRS is a Treasury bureau; recorded under Treasury per the agencies table. Distinct from the existing 'Treasury | ChatGPT Enterprise' entry (150-3,000 licenses); Agentforce is a separate, Salesforce-built agentic tool scoped to specific caseworking offices, not a general chat assistant.

findings.finding: SSA's HeaRT system uses generative AI to produce automated transcripts of disability-hearing recordings nationwide, projected to serve about 500,000 cases per year and save the agency about $5 million annually.
findings.estimated_users: ~500,000 cases/year across SSA hearing offices nationwide (a case-volume metric, not a headcount of individual tool users)
findings.exact_quote: Approximately 500,000 customers will benefit from this new software each year, and by fully utilizing HeaRT, SSA will save about $5 million per year.
findings.source_title: Social Security Announces AI Enhancements for Hearings Recordings | SSA
findings.notes: Direct fetch of ssa.gov returned HTTP 403; the exact quote was confirmed via a contemporaneous syndicated republish (stl.news) carrying identical verbatim text consistent with the official SSA press release dated 2025-03-13. HeaRT is a case-processing/transcription tool, not a general chat assistant — distinct from the existing 'SSA | Agency Support Companion (ASC)' entry, which is the agency's general-purpose employee chatbot.

findings.finding: DHSChat, DHS's internally built secure generative AI chatbot, launched to roughly 19,000 employees at DHS headquarters with pilot access for select users across ten operating agencies.
findings.estimated_users: ~19,000 DHS headquarters employees, plus select pilot users across 10 operating agencies (DHS workforce ~260,000 total)
findings.exact_quote: now available to all the roughly 19,000 employees at DHS headquarters and select pilot users across ten operating agencies.
findings.source_title: DHS launches internal GenAI chatbot to leverage non-public data | Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: Quote attributed to Michael Boyce, Director of the DHS AI Corps, in the tool's launch announcement. This is the first publicly source-cited anchor for the DHSChat HQ-launch figure; the existing 'DHS | DHSChat' entry's claim of department-wide 'all' coverage beyond this HQ launch rests on primary_attestation only (a program lead's first-hand account) pending public corroboration — this entry supplies the publicly documented baseline that claim builds on.

findings.tool_name: ChatGPT and Claude (commercial GenAI) — DHS enterprise access
findings.finding: DHS's CIO directed staff to stop using commercial generative AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude, reversing prior permissive use as the department pivoted to its in-house DHSChat.
findings.estimated_users: Restriction applied department-wide; affected employees who previously had commercial-AI access (DHS headquarters cohort was ~19,000-20,000)
findings.exact_quote: Staff at the Department of Homeland Security are no longer allowed to use commercial generative artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT and Claude, according to a memo sent to employees this month.
findings.source_title: Homeland Security cuts off access to ChatGPT and other commercial AI | FedScoop
findings.notes: Memo issued by DHS CIO Antoine McCord. Updates/complements the existing 'DHS | Commercial generative AI (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot Chat) - pre-DHSChat program' entry (coverage=partial, undated cutoff) with a dated, sourced policy reversal: as of May 2025, commercial GenAI access at DHS was formally revoked in favor of DHSChat.

findings.finding: GSA Deputy Administrator Michael Lynch reported that roughly 70% of GSA employees are consistent users of the agency's AI tools, crediting the adoption with hundreds of thousands of hours of automation and process-optimization savings.
findings.estimated_users: ~70% of GSA's ~13,000 employees are consistent AI tool users
findings.exact_quote: roughly 70% of GSA employees are consistent users of the tools
findings.source_title: GSA's AI adoption is driving significant time savings, officials say | Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: Attributed to GSA Deputy Administrator Michael Lynch; the article also cites ~400,000 hours of automation unlocked and ~500,000 hours identified via employee process-optimization. Distinct from the existing per-tool 'GSA | GSAi' entry (which covers the specific internal chatbot); this entry is a broader across-tools adoption-rate claim.

findings.finding: GSA's USAi platform now hosts AI-experimentation environments for more than 25 federal agencies, with 16 more agencies onboarding by the end of 2026 — up from the 15 agencies reported in GSA's April 2026 budget request.
findings.estimated_users: 25+ agencies currently hosted; 16 more onboarding by end of 2026
findings.exact_quote: host, currently, over 25 different agencies ... We are onboarding another 16 between now and the end of the year.
findings.source_title: GSA's AI adoption is driving significant time savings, officials say | Nextgov/FCW
findings.notes: Quote attributed to GSA Deputy Administrator Michael Lynch; minor verb-tense smoothing around 'host' to join two clauses from the same quote. Supersedes/extends the existing 'GSA | USAi.gov' entry's April 2026 figure of '15 agencies ... per GSA FY budget request' with a more current June 2026 count.

findings.tool_name: Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government (Anthropic OneGov agreement)
findings.finding: GSA's OneGov agreement makes Anthropic's Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government available to all three branches of the U.S. government for a nominal $1 fee for up to a year; per-agency adoption following the deal is not disclosed in the release.
findings.estimated_users: Procurement-availability offer to all federal civilian executive-branch agencies plus the legislative and judicial branches (not an adoption/usage count)
findings.exact_quote: Claude for Enterprise and Claude for Government to all three branches of the U.S. government — federal civilian executive, legislative, and judiciary
findings.source_title: GSA Strikes Another OneGov Deal with Anthropic to Offer Claude AI to all Branches of Gov for Just $1 | GSA
findings.notes: This is a government-wide procurement vehicle administered by GSA, not a GSA-employee-specific rollout; recorded under GSA as the announcing/administering agency. coverage_assessment set to 'unknown' because the release establishes availability/pricing, not confirmed per-agency uptake. Executive-branch agencies procure via GSA's Multiple Award Schedule; judicial/legislative branches use their own contract vehicles.

findings.finding: GSA's OneGov agreement makes OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise available to every participating federal agency for a nominal $1 fee for one year, plus 60 days of unlimited advanced-model use afterward.
findings.estimated_users: Procurement-availability offer to every participating federal agency (not an adoption/usage count)
findings.exact_quote: Every participating U.S. federal agency will have access for a nominal fee of $1 to ChatGPT Enterprise for one year.
findings.source_title: GSA Announces New Partnership with OpenAI, Delivering Deep Discount to ChatGPT Gov-Wide Through MAS | GSA
findings.notes: Government-wide procurement vehicle administered by GSA; recorded under GSA as announcing/administering agency, not a GSA-employee-specific rollout. Preceded the Anthropic OneGov deal by six days. coverage_assessment 'unknown' because this establishes pricing/availability, not confirmed uptake.

findings.finding: GSA's OneGov agreement with Microsoft makes Microsoft 365 Copilot available at no cost for up to 12 months to federal agencies holding Microsoft G5 licenses, as part of a package Microsoft says could save the government $3.1 billion in the first year.
findings.estimated_users: No-cost 12-month offer to Microsoft G5 license holders across federal agencies ('millions of existing Microsoft G5 users' per Microsoft); not an adoption/usage count
findings.exact_quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot available at no cost for up to 12 months for Microsoft G5 customers.
findings.source_title: Multi-Billion Dollar GSA OneGov Agreement with Microsoft Brings Steep Discounts for Microsoft 365, Copilot, and Azure Cloud Services | GSA
findings.notes: Government-wide procurement vehicle administered by GSA; recorded under GSA as announcing/administering agency, not a GSA-employee-specific rollout. Microsoft's own messaging characterizes the eligible pool as 'millions of existing Microsoft G5 users' government-wide. coverage_assessment 'unknown' because this establishes pricing/licensing terms, not confirmed uptake.
